extensionDescription.message: Lets AI assistants (MCP) search and write your Thunderbird mail, calendar, contacts and filters. Runs on this computer only.
extensionDescription.description: Description of the add-on in the Add-ons Manager (manifest.json). At most 132 characters.

pageLanguage.description: Language code of this translation (the lang attribute of the options page). Not shown as text.

pageTitle.description: Title of the options tab. Keep the add-on name "Commonpost MCP for Thunderbird" as is.

pageTagline.message: Lets AI assistants (MCP) work with your mail, calendar, contacts and filters. The add-on runs on this computer; what the assistant reads goes to the AI app you connect.
pageTagline.description: Line under the add-on name at the top of the options page.

autoSaveNote.message: Each change is saved as soon as you make it.
autoSaveNote.description: Under the page title: there is no Save button.

statusHeading.description: Heading of the server status section.

fullAccessSummary.description: Folded note in the status section, about the line Thunderbird shows in the add-on's Permissions tab. Quote Thunderbird's own wording in your language.

fullAccessWhy.message: Thunderbird shows that line for every add-on built on an Experiment, whatever the add-on does: an add-on cannot change or narrow it. This one needs an Experiment for its local server, message filters and the calendar.
fullAccessWhy.description: Body of the note, first paragraph.

fullAccessWhat.message: What it does with it: by default it listens on this computer only, behind a token; it writes files only in its own temporary folder; its code makes no Internet request. What the assistant reads goes to the AI app you connect, and nowhere else.
fullAccessWhat.description: Body of the note, second paragraph.

retryFailed.description: Status after Retry start failed; $ERROR$ is the reason (English, from the add-on).

bridgeHeading.description: Heading of the Bridge section. The bridge is mcp-bridge.cjs, the program each AI app runs to reach Thunderbird.

bridgeIntro.message: Each AI app connects through its own copy of the bridge (mcp-bridge.cjs, or the .mcpb bundle in Claude Desktop). The bridge lives in that app and is not updated with this add-on: this section tells you when one needs replacing. Bridges that connected since Thunderbird started:
bridgeIntro.description: Introduction of the Bridge section; the list of bridges follows.

bridgeEmpty.message: No bridge has connected since Thunderbird started.
bridgeEmpty.description: Shown when the list of bridges is empty.

refresh.description: Button that reads the list of bridges again.

bridgeThresholdWithVersion.message: This add-on (version $VERSION$) recommends bridge $MIN$ or newer.
bridgeThresholdWithVersion.description: First sentence above the list of bridges. $VERSION$: version of the add-on; $MIN$: lowest recommended bridge version.

bridgeThreshold.message: This add-on recommends bridge $MIN$ or newer.
bridgeThreshold.description: First sentence above the list of bridges when the add-on version is unknown. $MIN$: lowest recommended bridge version.

bridgeThresholdFloor.description: Sentence after the first one. $FLOOR$: lowest bridge version that works at all.

bridgeThresholdPublished.message: The bridge published with it is $VERSION$.
bridgeThresholdPublished.description: Sentence after the first one. $VERSION$: version of the bridge released with this add-on.

bridgeLineVersion.description: Line of a bridge entry. $VERSION$: its version, or a word such as "unreadable".

bridgeVersionNotReported.message: not reported (bridge 0.11 or older, or another HTTP client)
bridgeVersionNotReported.description: Bridge version: the client sent none.

bridgeVersionUnreadable.description: Bridge version: the one sent cannot be read.

bridgeLineInstalledAs.description: Line of a bridge entry. $PACKAGING$: how the bridge is installed.

bridgePackagingMcpb.description: How a bridge is installed: the bundle of Claude Desktop.

bridgePackagingFile.description: How a bridge is installed: the file mcp-bridge.cjs.

bridgePackagingUnknown.description: How a bridge is installed: not known.

bridgeLineProfile.description: Line of a bridge entry. $PROFILE$: the Thunderbird profile the bridge asked for.

bridgeLineProfileInvalid.description: Line of a bridge entry whose profile name is not valid.

bridgeLineLastSeen.description: Line of a bridge entry. $DATE$: date and time of its last request.

bridgeLineStatus.description: Line of a bridge entry. $STATUS$: one of the bridge states.

bridgeStateNewerAvailable.message: Newer version available: this bridge works, the update is optional.

bridgeStateNewerAvailableVersion.message: Newer version available ($VERSION$): this bridge works, the update is optional.
bridgeStateNewerAvailableVersion.description: Bridge state, with the newest version.

bridgeStateUnversioned.message: Update recommended: this bridge does not report a readable version.

bridgeStateRefused.message: Refused: older than the security floor of this add-on (no tool works with it).

bridgeStateNewerThanAddOn.message: Newer than this add-on: in Add-ons and Themes, choose Check for Updates in the gear menu, then restart Thunderbird.
bridgeStateNewerThanAddOn.description: Bridge state. Use Thunderbird's own names of the Add-ons Manager and of its Check for Updates menu item.

bridgeToUpdate.description: Line before the update steps of a bridge.

bridgeStepDownload.description: First update step. $FILE$: a link named after the file.

bridgeStepDownloadMcpbFromRelease.message: Download the .mcpb bundle from the release of this add-on, on the Releases page of github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp.
bridgeStepDownloadMcpbFromRelease.description: First update step when no direct link can be given. Releases is the name of the GitHub page.

bridgeStepDownloadFileFromRelease.message: Download mcp-bridge.cjs from the release of this add-on, on the Releases page of github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp.
bridgeStepDownloadFileFromRelease.description: First update step when no direct link can be given. Releases is the name of the GitHub page.

bridgeStepMcpbOpen.message: Open the downloaded file with Claude Desktop: it replaces the installed bundle. If it does not open there (Windows), use Settings > Extensions > Advanced settings > Install Extension.
bridgeStepMcpbOpen.description: Update step of a .mcpb bundle. The menu path is Claude Desktop's; keep it as Claude Desktop shows it.

bridgeStepFileReplace.message: Put the downloaded file in place of the $FILE$ that your MCP client starts: same name, same folder.
bridgeStepFileReplace.description: Update step of mcp-bridge.cjs. $FILE$: the file name, shown as code.

bridgeWhereClaudeCode.message: Claude Code: $LIST$ names the server, $GET$ shows the path.
bridgeWhereClaudeCode.description: How to find the file in Claude Code. $LIST$ and $GET$: commands, shown as code.

bridgeWhereOtherClients.message: Other clients: the path is in the arguments of the server, in the MCP configuration of the client.
bridgeWhereOtherClients.description: How to find the file in other MCP clients.

bridgeStepRestart.message: Restart the MCP client, or reconnect the server (in Claude Code: $COMMAND$).
bridgeStepRestart.description: Last update step. $COMMAND$: a command, shown as code.

bridgePluginNote.message: Claude Code with the Commonpost plugin: nothing to download. Run $UPDATE$, then $RELOAD$.
bridgePluginNote.description: Note under the update steps of mcp-bridge.cjs. $UPDATE$ and $RELOAD$: commands, shown as code.

safetyHeading.description: Heading of the send safety section.

safetyIntro.message: What the assistant may do on its own, and what waits for you: mail, calendar, filter rules.
safetyIntro.description: Introduction of the send safety section.

reviewMailTitle.message: Mail: review every message before it is sent
reviewMailTitle.description: Checkbox: mail is sent only from a compose window the user checks. "Mail:" tells it apart from the calendar checkbox below.

reviewMailHelpOn.message: Checked: the assistant fills in a compose window; you read it and press Send.
reviewMailHelpOn.description: Help of the checkbox, checked state. Send is the button of Thunderbird's compose window.

reviewMailHelpOff.message: Unchecked: it can send mail by itself.
reviewMailHelpOff.description: Help of the checkbox, unchecked state.

reviewCalendarTitle.message: Calendar: review every event and task it creates
reviewCalendarTitle.description: Checkbox: events and tasks are created only from Thunderbird's dialog.

reviewCalendarHelpOn.message: Checked: Thunderbird's own dialog opens filled in, and the item exists once you save it in that dialog.
reviewCalendarHelpOn.description: Help of the checkbox, checked state.

reviewCalendarHelpOff.message: Unchecked (the default for a new installation): events and tasks are added to the calendar at once. Nobody is invited, but people the calendar is shared with see them.
reviewCalendarHelpOff.description: Help of the checkbox, unchecked state.

reviewCalendarHelpChanges.message: Changing or deleting an existing event or task never opens a dialog, checked or not.
reviewCalendarHelpChanges.description: Help of the checkbox: what it does not cover.

technicalDetails.description: Folded section with details for MCP client developers.

safetyTechSend1.message: While the first setting is on, MCP clients asking for a direct send are rejected:
safetyTechSend1.description: Technical details, part 1; the code skipReview: true follows.

safetyTechSend2.message: on sendMail, replyToMessage or forwardMessage, and
safetyTechSend2.description: Technical details, part 2, after the code skipReview: true; the code mode: "send" follows. Keep the tool names as is.

safetyTechSend3.message: on replyToMessage or forwardMessage; the review window remains available.
safetyTechSend3.description: Technical details, part 3, after the code mode: "send"; the code mode: "draft" follows.

safetyTechSend4.message: only saves a draft, sends nothing and is not blocked (it needs the saveDraft tool under Tool Access).
safetyTechSend4.description: Technical details, part 4, after the code mode: "draft". Tool Access is the section of this page.

safetyTechCalendar1.message: While the second setting is on, createEvent and createTask open Thunderbird's dialog and

filterSendRuleHeading.message: Filter rules that send mail (forward / reply)
filterSendRuleHeading.description: Heading of the setting about filter rules that forward or reply.

filterSendRuleIntro.message: A filter rule that forwards or replies sends mail by itself, every time, without review. A message the assistant reads could trick it into asking for one.

filterBlockTitle.description: Choice: the assistant can never create a rule that sends mail.

filterBlockHelp.message: The assistant can never create such rules, nor change or run a filter list that holds one; deleting one stays possible. Make these rules yourself in Thunderbird's filter editor.

filterConfirmTitle.description: Choice: Thunderbird asks the user before such a rule is written.

filterConfirmHelp1.message: Thunderbird shows you the account, the rule and where it sends mail. Nothing is written unless you confirm;
filterConfirmHelp1.description: Help of the choice, part 1; the button name Refuse follows (in English, as the dialog shows it).

filterConfirmHelp2.message: is the default button (Enter and Escape refuse), and the question expires after 10 minutes.
filterConfirmHelp2.description: Help of the choice, part 2, after the button name Refuse.

filterTech1.message: Whatever the setting: rules that send mail on outgoing mail are refused, and MCP clients can never accept a confirmation themselves. One request at a time, at most 5 per hour. Every request and answer is recorded in
filterTech1.description: Technical details, part 1; the file name commonpost-mcp-confirmations.log follows.

filterTech2.message: in your profile folder (no message content).
filterTech2.description: Technical details, part 2, after the file name.

encryptedHeading.description: Heading of the encrypted messages section.

encryptedIntro.message: OpenPGP and S/MIME messages stay private by default: the assistant only learns that a message is encrypted, and replyToMessage / forwardMessage do not send one without review.
encryptedIntro.description: Introduction of the section. Keep the tool names as is.

encryptedTitle.message: Let the assistant read encrypted messages

encryptedHelp1.message: Thunderbird then decrypts them for the tools, and
encryptedHelp1.description: Help of the checkbox, part 1; a bold part follows.

encryptedHelp2.message: their content goes to the assistant, and so to the service that runs it
encryptedHelp2.description: Help of the checkbox, part 2 (bold); a period follows.

advancedIntro.message: Leave these as they are unless you know you need them.

listenAllTitle.description: Checkbox: the server accepts connections from other devices.

listenAllHelp.message: By default only this computer can connect to the server.

listenAllWarning.message: Every device on your network can then reach the server, over plain HTTP: the access token travels in clear text and anyone there can read it, and the check of the Host header is off in this mode. Turn it on only on a network you fully trust, and off again when you no longer need it.
listenAllWarning.description: Warning shown while the checkbox is on. Keep Host (an HTTP header name) as is.

currentTokenLabel.description: Label of the access token of the running server.

notAvailable.description: Placeholder of the token field when there is no token.

copied.description: Status after the token was copied.

stableTokenTitle.description: Checkbox: keep the same access token across restarts.

stableTokenHelp.message: Keeps the same token across restarts, for MCP clients you configure by hand. Changes apply the next time the server starts.

stableTokenBefore.message: Before you use a stable token
stableTokenBefore.description: Folded warning about the stable token.

stableTokenWarning.message: The token is stored in your Thunderbird profile. If it becomes known to someone else it stays valid until you regenerate it or uncheck "Use stable token". Removing the add-on while it is enabled clears the stored token; if you disable the add-on first, uncheck "Use stable token" before removing it, since removing an already-disabled add-on leaves the token in the profile.
stableTokenWarning.description: Warning about the stable token. "Use stable token" is the checkbox title (stableTokenTitle).

stableTokenLabel.description: Label of the stable token field.

generate.description: Button that makes a new random stable token.

regenerate.description: Button that replaces the stable token by a new one.

generatedTokenEmpty.description: Error: the add-on returned an empty token.

generatedAndSaved.description: Status after a stable token was made and saved.

regeneratedAndSaved.description: Status after the stable token was replaced and saved.

stableTokenCleared.description: Status after the stable token was removed.
